Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst case for a single operation occurs when a vertex has the maximum possible out-degree, which in a simple directed graph is |V| - 1. The aggregate amortized cost is derived by summing all operation costs and dividing by the total number of operations.

* (a) The cost of the worst possible single operation is **|V| - 1**, since a vertex can have at most |V| - 1 outgoing edges in a simple directed graph (one edge to each of the other vertices).
* (b) The average amortized cost based on aggregate analysis is **|E| / |V|**, because the total cost of all |V| operations equals the sum of all out-degrees, which equals |E| (the total number of edges), and we divide by the |V| operations to get the amortized cost per operation.
